title: AALP interface v1
description: Provider-agnostic external-API transport service, exposed to cross-protocol clients (primarily ACP) without depending on any AALP-private Python module, class, or on-disk state. This is the sole cross-protocol-supported surface of AALP; it deliberately excludes AALP's own administrative/credential functionality.

excluded_from_this_interface.credential.read: AALP-owned administrative functionality. Never exposed to cross-protocol clients through interface v1, in any form.
excluded_from_this_interface.request.batch: Deferred. No genuine finite-batch need has been demonstrated by ACP yet; may become a new, additive, capability-gated operation in a later interface_version 1.x once one is.

authentication.mechanism: single bearer secret over a loopback Unix domain socket
authentication.notes: AALP has exactly one authorized client per host (ACP). The bearer secret is transport/session bootstrap material, not a per-request credential, and is out of scope for this document's field-level schemas. It is never a provider credential and this interface never exposes provider credentials (see excluded_from_this_interface).

bootstrap.summary: How a client discovers where AALP is listening and what bearer secret to send, without reading any other AALP-private on-disk state.

descriptor_file.aalp_root_resolution: AALP_HOME environment variable if set, else the current working directory AALP was started from. A client must be told this root out-of-band (e.g. via shared deployment configuration); interface v1 defines no discovery operation for locating an unknown root.

format.socket_path: string, absolute filesystem path to the bound AF_UNIX socket
format.secret_file: string, absolute path to the bearer secret file

descriptor_file.written: atomically, by AALP's ingress on startup, before it begins accepting connections

secret_file.format: opaque bearer token, raw bytes, no trailing newline guaranteed
secret_file.permissions: 0600, owner-only, generated once by AALP and never transmitted except as the value clients send back inside the request envelope's Authorization header field
secret_file.usage: sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <contents>' (a field inside the JSON request envelope, not an HTTP header) on every request.forward / provider.status / service.capabilities call

bootstrap.carve_out_rationale: These two files exist specifically so a cross-protocol client can bootstrap a connection without a hardcoded socket path or a pre-shared secret out-of-band. They are the one deliberate, narrow exception to the 'never read another protocol's private state' rule (adjustment metadata §4): a client may read exactly these two paths, for exactly this purpose, and must not read or infer anything else from '.aalp/' state. Everything else under '.aalp/' (credentials, audit log, provider lane internals) remains off-limits.

transport_binding.notes: request.forward's binding below is AALP's existing, already-implemented wire protocol and is normative: a conforming AALP service and a conforming fake service used for ACP client tests must both implement it exactly as described. provider.status and service.capabilities are new discovery operations required by this interface; the method/path pairs given below are the concrete binding a fake service and the real AALP service must both implement, but a different transport encoding could replace the envelope format in a later interface_version without changing the operation names, fields, or outcome semantics documented here.

wire_protocol.socket: AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, bound at the path published in the bootstrap descriptor
wire_protocol.framing: Each connection carries exactly one request and one response, then closes. A request or response is one frame: a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length prefix, followed by that many bytes of UTF-8-encoded JSON.

request_envelope.headers: object of string to string, includes 'Authorization' and, for request.forward, optionally 'X-Aalp-Flow-Id'
request_envelope.body: string, base64-encoded request body bytes (empty string if there is no body)

response_envelope.headers: object of string to string, includes 'X-Aalp-Outcome' for request.forward responses
response_envelope.body: string, base64-encoded response body bytes (empty string if there is no body)

wire_protocol.deadline_handling: AALP's ingress imposes no read/write deadline of its own; all queue_timeout/compression_timeout/total_timeout budget enforcement is the client's responsibility, tracked as a single cumulative deadline across however many individual socket reads/writes one call takes -- never a single per-syscall timeout, which cannot bound a multi-syscall read.

transport_binding.reserved_path_prefix_rule: No provider id may begin with '_'. This keeps discovery paths under /_aalp/v1/... from ever colliding with request.forward's /{provider_id}/... passthrough paths.

scheduling_model.description: Requests targeting the same provider are served strictly in the order they are submitted to that provider, independent of which logical flow/caller/agent submitted them. There is no round robin, no priority, no per-agent fairness, and no idle reservation of a future request's turn. This ordering guarantee is per-provider, not a single global queue: different providers' requests may execute concurrently, and once a provider's concurrency_limit is greater than 1, that provider's own requests may too (see concurrency_bound below) -- FIFO order applies among requests contending for the same provider slot(s), not as a system-wide single-flight bottleneck.

flow_id.semantics: A purely optional audit/grouping label. It confers no scheduling priority and does not let anything reserve capacity for a later, not-yet-submitted request. Two requests sharing the same flow_id are not guaranteed to run adjacently, and a request with no flow_id is scheduled exactly like one that has it.

scheduling_model.renewal_operation_notes: Interface v1 defines no renewal, lease-extension, or open-ended reservation operation of any kind. A caller cannot reserve a lane slot ahead of submitting the request that will use it.
scheduling_model.concurrency_bound: Per active provider's declared concurrency_limit, discoverable via provider.status. The default 'ci' provider is concurrency_limit 1 (single-flight): AALP never starts a new upstream request for a provider beyond that provider's declared ceiling, and a caller's local timeout never by itself frees a slot that a not-yet-confirmed-closed upstream operation may still be occupying.

outcomes.description: The closed set of outcomes request.forward may report, reusing aalp.errors.Outcome verbatim. No cross-protocol client should ever need to handle a value outside this set for request.forward, and no future v1.x addition may repurpose one of these values to mean something else.

success.meaning: The request reached the provider and a response was read back completely. The upstream HTTP status code (e.g. a provider-side 4xx/5xx) is preserved as-is in the response and is NOT itself a non-success AALP outcome — AALP classifies only transport-level results, never the provider's own application-level response.
success.response_status_code: passthrough (identical to the upstream response's status code)

unavailable.meaning: The target provider id is unknown or is currently marked inactive (providers/*.json 'active': false). No upstream network attempt was made.

queue_timeout.meaning: The request could not be admitted into its target provider's own FIFO lane before its queue-timeout budget elapsed. No upstream network attempt was made.

compression_timeout.meaning: An upstream network attempt was made and a connection-level timeout occurred while sending the request or reading the response (the upstream's own per-request timeout budget, distinct from the queue-wait budget).

total_timeout.meaning: The request's overall (queue + upstream) timeout budget elapsed. May occur either before an upstream attempt started (if admission alone exhausted the budget) or immediately after a lane slot was confirmed idle before any attempt was made.

invalid_response.meaning: An upstream network attempt was made and a connection was established, but the response could not be read/parsed as a well-formed HTTP response.

upstream_error.meaning: An upstream network attempt failed at the connection/transport level (DNS, TCP, TLS, or protocol-level failure) before any response was read.

service.capabilities.summary: Discover AALP's interface version and capability set.

capabilities.description: See top-level 'capabilities'. Absence of a capability string means a client must not assume that behavior is supported, even if it appears elsewhere in this document as a v1 concept (e.g. 'request.batch' is deliberately never present).

outcomes.note: Not modeled with the request.forward Outcome enum. A reachable AALP service always returns 200 with the body above; only a transport-level failure to reach the service at all (connection refused, etc.) is possible, and is not an AALP-level outcome.

provider.status.summary: Discover provider availability, concurrency state, and accepted request shape, so a client never needs to read providers/*.json directly.

provider_id.description: When present (single form), scopes the response to one provider. When absent (list form), returns every provider AALP has loaded, active or not.

active.description: Whether request.forward will attempt this provider at all; false yields outcome 'unavailable'.

concurrency_limit.description: Maximum simultaneous in-flight upstream requests AALP will ever hold open for this provider.

in_flight.description: Currently held provider-lane leases (upstream requests in progress, including quarantined/unconfirmed-closed ones).

queued.description: Requests currently waiting in this provider's FIFO lane.

accepted_paths.description: The exact upstream request paths request.forward will accept for this provider (the second path segment onward). Any other path yields outcome 'unavailable' for that provider.

explicitly_excluded_fields: endpoint (AALP-internal upstream URL; not needed to use request.forward, and not exposed)

outcomes.note: Not modeled with the request.forward Outcome enum; plain HTTP 200 / 404 as above.

request.forward.summary: Submit one provider request and receive a documented outcome. The only operation that talks to a provider's upstream API.

binding.path_notes: The first '/'-delimited path segment names the target provider id and is stripped before forwarding; everything after it must exactly match one of that provider's accepted_paths (see provider.status).

provider_id.description: Taken from the path, not a header or body field.

path.description: Must be one of the target provider's accepted_paths.

X-Aalp-Flow-Id.description: Optional. See scheduling_model.flow_id. Never required, never a scheduling reservation.

headers.description: Forwarded upstream verbatim, except the provider's own declared auth header, which AALP overwrites with the credential it holds; a client must never attempt to set that header itself to authenticate with the provider.

body.description: Raw request body, forwarded upstream byte-for-byte unmodified on outcome 'success'.

on_outcome_success.headers: passthrough (upstream response headers, verbatim) plus X-Aalp-Outcome: success

message.description: Non-normative diagnostic text; clients must key behavior off 'outcome', never off this string.

x_aalp_outcome_header.rationale: On outcome 'success', AALP passes the upstream status code through verbatim — including a provider-side 4xx/5xx, which is a valid AALP-level success. Status code alone therefore cannot disambiguate an AALP-level failure (e.g. 502 upstream_error) from a provider that itself happened to return 502. X-Aalp-Outcome removes that ambiguity and must be present on every request.forward response, success or not.

compatibility.versioning: Interface major versions are protocol-local to AALP; they need not match ACP's or ADP's interface version numbers.
stays_within_current_major_version_when_: existing outcomes retain their documented meaning
existing clients keep working without adopting any new capability
new fields are optional and/or gated behind a new capability string
service.capabilities exposes any newly added capability
requires_a_new_major_version_when_any_of: an operation or field is removed or renamed
an existing operation's or outcome's semantics change incompatibly
a previously valid request becomes invalid
